items.title: The Lost Book of Moses: The Hunt for the World's Oldest Bible
items.note: Journalistic investigation of Shapira's career and of the fate of the fragments after their 1885 sale, which renewed public interest in the case.

items.title: The Shapira Scroll was an Authentic Dead Sea Scroll
items.note: Argued from circumstantial evidence about the reported find and the condition of the strips that they came from a cave near the Dead Sea.

items.title: The Valediction of Moses: A Proto-Biblical Book
items.note: Open-access edition and commentary arguing that the text is an antecedent of Deuteronomy rather than a reworking of it.

items.title: The Moses Scroll
items.note: Popular reconstruction and translation arguing for authenticity, with contributions by James D. Tabor.

items.title: The Valediction of Moses: New Evidence on the Shapira Deuteronomy Fragments
items.note: Presented Shapira's working transcription from a Berlin State Library inventory, whose corrections Dershowitz read as Shapira struggling with a text he had not composed.

items.title: The "Valediction of Moses" is not a proto-Deuteronomy: evidence from the verbal system
items.note: Argues that the mix of Classical and non-Classical Hebrew verb forms in the strips points to a modern composition, not a pre-exilic source.

items.title: Notes on the Orthography of the Shapira Manuscripts: The Forger's Marks
items.note: Argued that the spelling mixes Mesha stele and biblical conventions, including consistent waw for final ō, an anachronism for an ancient scribe.

items.title: Zur »Valediction of Moses«
items.note: Short reply arguing that twentieth-century finds and research vindicate Hermann Guthe's 1883 scepticism about the fragments.

items.title: The Shapira Scrolls: The Case for Authenticity
items.who: I. Dershowitz and J. D. Tabor
items.note: Popular statement of the authenticity case, printed alongside Hendel and Richelle's case for forgery.

items.title: The Shapira Scrolls: The Case for Forgery
items.note: Summarized the orthographic and palaeographic case against authenticity, drawing on the British Library file.

items.title: Moses Wilhelm Shapira's "Deuteronomy" between Epigraphy and Literary Criticism
items.note: Weighs the epigraphic and literary-critical arguments raised since Dershowitz's revival of the case.

items.title: Shapira's Deuteronomy, Its Decalogue, and Dead Sea Scrolls Authentic and Forged
items.note: Compared the text with the Dead Sea Scrolls and known forgeries and proposed it is a post-biblical pastiche from nineteenth-century Jerusalem.

items.title: The Career of Moses Shapira, Bookseller and Antiquarian
items.note: Surveys Shapira's whole career as dealer, setting the Deuteronomy strips and Moabite pottery within his methods and the Ottoman Palestine antiquities trade.

items.title: The Valediction of Moses: A Proto-Biblical Book by Idan Dershowitz (review)
items.note: Extended review of the monograph weighing its central hypothesis against the palaeographic, linguistic and historical objections.

items.title: A Text That Was but Isn't: On the Contribution of Literary Evidence in the Assessment of Shapira Deuteronomy
items.note: Argued that the text responds to a compiled Pentateuch, which tells against Dershowitz's proto-biblical reading.

items.title: The Magic of Forgery: Patterns of Distraction in the Authentication of Suspicious Objects
items.note: Catalogues recurrent arguments in academic authentications of biblical forgeries, with the Shapira revival among its cases.

items.title: Moses Wilhelm Shapira, Hermann Weser and the Moab Expedition: Provenance Study of the Moabitica
items.note: Ceramic petrography and XRF on Shapira's Moabite pottery, combined with the German expedition's records, to trace where the forgeries were made.

items.title: Did the Shapira manuscript betray an unambiguously Pentateuchal perspective? A rejoinder to Stackert
items.who: A. D. Friedberg and J. Hoppe
items.venue: Journal for the Study of the Old Testament
items.note: Replies that independent traditions could explain Stackert's parallels and that the text may draw on an earlier form of the Pentateuch.

items.title: Biblical Forgery and Academic Authentication: Persisting Patterns of Guile and Gullibility
items.note: Monograph on scholars' role in authenticating biblical forgeries, treating recent re-evaluations of the Shapira manuscripts as one case.
